findings.title: Retry-count delete branch can delete non-SMS reminders
findings.body: The new second OR branch only checks `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`, unlike the first branch which filters `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. `WorkflowReminder` is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP methods, so any non-SMS reminder with `retryCount > 1` would be deleted by this SMS cron job. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and likely `scheduled: false`) to this branch to prevent deleting unrelated workflow reminders.

findings.title: retryCount increments are not atomic
findings.body: Both update sites use `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` based on the value read earlier by `findMany`. If two cron invocations overlap, they can both read the same value and write the same value, losing an increment. This can defeat the delete-after-two-failures logic and may allow more retries or duplicate Twilio schedule calls than intended. Use an atomic `increment: 1` update instead.

findings.title: All errors count as SMS scheduling failures
findings.body: The try block includes reminder preparation work such as `getBookerBaseUrl` (line 119) and `bookingMetadataSchema.parse` (line 134) before Twilio is called. The catch at line 190 increments `retryCount` for any error in that block. As a result, a record with malformed booking metadata can throw during parsing each run, reach retryCount 2, and then be deleted at the start of a later run even though no SMS scheduling was ever attempted and the event is still upcoming. Only `twilio.scheduleSMS` failures should count toward this deletion limit, or preparation errors should be handled separately.
